tasks.title: Fix it: a private function of a module
tasks.statement: In the module bank the functions new_account and deposit are not marked pub, and the code outside the module does not build (E0603). Open to the outside exactly what the driver needs: new_account and deposit. Leave the field balance private: the balance can be read only through audit.
tasks.hint: The word pub before fn: new_account and deposit become visible from outside the module.

tasks.title: Private fields: constructor and getters
tasks.statement: The fields of Rect are private, so from outside the struct can be neither built nor read. Write new(w, h) → Result<Rect, String> (the sides must be > 0, otherwise the error «side must be positive»), width(), height(), area() and scale(&self, k: u32) → Rect.
tasks.hint: The constructor is the only way to get a Rect from outside; so inside it you can guarantee w > 0 and h > 0.

tasks.title: Fix it: the trait is not in scope
tasks.statement: The trait Shout is implemented for str in the module text, but the method shout() cannot be called in the function loud: the trait name is not imported (E0599). Fix it with a single use line.
tasks.hint: Trait methods are available only if the trait itself is imported: use text::Shout;

tasks.title: pub use: a flat public interface
tasks.statement: The types Circle and Rect lie deep: shapes::circle::Circle and shapes::rect::Rect, and the trait Shape is in shapes::Shape. Make Circle, Rect and Shape available from the crate root (pub use), and also a module prelude with the same three names.
tasks.hint: In the root: pub use shapes::circle::Circle; and so on; prelude is a module with pub use crate::{…}.

tasks.title: Paths: crate, self, super
tasks.statement: Three nested modules. util::double(x) → x * 2. engine::run(x) → util::double(x) + 1 (a path from the root). engine::fast::run(x) → engine::run(x) through super, and fast::twice(x) → self::step(x) * 2. Implement the functions using exactly these paths: crate::, super::, self::.
tasks.hint: Three different path beginnings: crate::util::double, super::run, self::step — once each.

tasks.title: use std::fmt::Write for String
tasks.statement: render_table(rows: &[(&str, i32)]) → String: lines of the form name<padded with spaces to 8>|<number right-aligned to width 5> with a newline; at the end a line «total» with the sum. Build the result with writeln! directly into the String (for this you need to import the trait std::fmt::Write).
tasks.hint: writeln!(out, "...") is available on String only if use std::fmt::Write is imported; the result needs unwrap() or ?.

tasks.title: An invariant in the constructor: Kelvin
tasks.statement: In the module temp the type Kelvin(f64) with a private field. new(k) → Result<Kelvin, String> (the error «below absolute zero: K»), from_celsius(c) → Result, kelvin(), celsius(), add(&self, delta: f64) → Result<Kelvin, String> (the sum must not go below zero). From outside it is impossible to get a value below zero.
tasks.hint: Every way to create a value goes through new: that is where the check k >= 0 lives.

tasks.title: A builder with validation in build()
tasks.statement: Config { host, port, tls, timeout_ms }. ConfigBuilder::new(host) with defaults (port 80, tls false, timeout 1000); the methods port(self, p), tls(self, on), timeout_ms(self, t) return Self; build(self) → Result<Config, String>: errors «empty host», «port 0», «timeout greater 60000»; if tls = true and the port is 80, the port automatically becomes 443.
tasks.hint: The setting methods return self, and all checks are gathered in build.

tasks.title: Default and struct update
tasks.statement: Config { name, retries, verbose, ratio, tags }. Implement Default by hand: name "app", retries 3, verbose false, ratio 0.5, tags empty. overridden(base, retries: Option<u32>, verbose: Option<bool>) → Config — put the given values on top of base (None — keep as it was).
tasks.hint: Config { retries: …, verbose: …, ..base } — the other fields are taken from base (including the string and the vector — they move).

tasks.title: Version: parsing, ordering, output
tasks.statement: Version { major, minor, patch } (u32). Implement FromStr for "1.2.3" (exactly three numbers, otherwise Err with the word «format»; a non-number → Err «number: <part>», with the offending part), Display "1.2.3" and ordering (derive Ord over the fields major, minor, patch). Then sort() and max() work.
tasks.hint: split('.') and a length check; parse the numbers in a closure with map_err and the ? operator.

tasks.title: Version requirements: ^, ~, =, >=
tasks.statement: Req::parse(s) → Option<Req> and matches(&self, v: &Version) → bool. "^1.2.3": ≥1.2.3 and <2.0.0 (for 0.x: "^0.2.3" — <0.3.0, "^0.0.3" — only 0.0.3); "~1.2.3": ≥1.2.3 and <1.3.0; "=1.2.3" — exactly; ">=1.2.3"; "*" — any. Version and version parsing are already done.
tasks.hint: For the caret there are three cases: major > 0 — major matches; otherwise minor > 0 — 0 and minor match; otherwise — only the exact version.

tasks.title: Bumping a version and compatibility
tasks.statement: bump(v: Version, kind: &str) → Option<Version>: "major" (minor and patch → 0), "minor" (patch → 0), "patch"; any other word — None. breaking(old, new) → bool: true if major grew, or major = 0 and minor grew. sort_desc(Vec<Version>) → Vec<Version> — from newest to oldest.
tasks.hint: The struct update Version { patch: …, ..v } changes only the listed fields.

tasks.title: Parsing Cargo.toml
tasks.statement: parse_manifest(text) → Result<Manifest, String>. Manifest { name, version, deps: BTreeMap<String, String> }. Sections [package] (name, version — in quotes) and [dependencies] (name = "version" or name = { version = "version", … }). Skip "#" comments and empty lines; ignore other sections. A missing name or version → Err("no name") / Err("no version").
tasks.hint: Remember the current section in a variable; get a quoted value with strip_prefix('"') and strip_suffix('"').

tasks.title: Crate build order
tasks.statement: build_order(deps: &[(&str, &[&str])]) → Result<Vec<String>, String>: each pair is a crate and its dependencies. Dependencies are built first; among the crates ready to build take them alphabetically. A dependency that is not in the list is considered external and is ignored. A cycle → Err("loop: a b c") with the remaining crates in alphabetical order.
tasks.hint: BTreeMap keys go alphabetically — the first crate with no remaining dependencies is the next one.

tasks.title: Features: the closure of enabled ones
tasks.statement: resolve(features: &[(&str, &[&str])], requested: &[&str]) → Result<Vec<String>, String>. Each feature enables others. The result is all enabled features alphabetically (including nested ones); "default" is always enabled if it is described. An unknown name in requested or in a dependency → Err("no feature X").
tasks.hint: Traverse with a stack and a set of already enabled ones; on an unknown name return the error at once.

tasks.title: Comparing Cargo.lock
tasks.statement: diff(old, new: &[(&str, &str)]) → Vec<String> — pairs (crate, version). In alphabetical order of crates: "+ name version" — appeared; "- name version" — disappeared; "~ name old -> new" — the version changed. Do not output unchanged ones.
tasks.hint: Merge the names of both lists into a BTreeSet — you get alphabetical order; then match on the pair of Options.

tasks.title: cfg!: what is known at build time
tasks.statement: build_info() → String of the form "mode=<debug|release> os=<linux|other> ptr=<32|64> endian=<little|big> unix=<yes|no>". Use the cfg! macro (debug_assertions, target_os = "linux", target_pointer_width, target_endian, unix). The check is built with optimization.
tasks.hint: cfg!(condition) is an ordinary boolean expression evaluated at build time; pairs like target_os = "linux".

tasks.title: Global state: AtomicUsize and OnceLock
tasks.statement: static NEXT: AtomicUsize — next_id() hands out 1, 2, 3, … (fetch_add), reset_ids() zeroes it, peek_id() shows the next one without handing it out. static NAME: OnceLock<String> — init_name(s) → bool: true if this is the first initialization; name() → Option<&'static str>.
tasks.hint: fetch_add returns the previous value; OnceLock::set returns Err if the value is already set.

tasks.title: const fn: tables at build time
tasks.statement: const fn fact(n: u32) → u64 (a while loop inside const fn is allowed). const FACTS: [u64; 11] — the factorials 0..=10, filled at build time through a const block. const fn gcd(a, b) → u64 (Euclid). const fn is_pow2(x: u32) → bool. The table and the functions are evaluated by the compiler.
tasks.hint: In const fn there is no for or closures — only while, let mut and arithmetic; a const block fills the table.

tasks.title: Mini rustdoc: extract documentation
tasks.statement: extract_docs(src: &str) → Vec<(String, String)>: for each function (fn name(… or pub fn name(…) collect the text of the "///" lines before it (without "///" and the space after it, joined with a space). Skip functions without documentation. Keep the order of the source.
tasks.hint: Accumulate /// lines in a vector; on a line with fn — save and clear; an attribute #[...] between the documentation and the function does not reset it.

tasks.title: A mini test runner
tasks.statement: type TestFn = fn() → Result<(), String>. run_tests(tests: &[(&str, TestFn)]) → (usize, usize, Vec<String>): the number passed, the number failed, and report lines "test <name> ... ok" / "test <name> ... FAILED: <message>". A panic inside a test is also a failure: "FAILED: panicked" (catch it with std::panic::catch_unwind). The runner itself must not crash.
tasks.hint: catch_unwind(*t) returns Result<Result<(), String>, Box<dyn Any + Send>>: three cases — ok, Err and panic.

tasks.title: Your own checks that return Result
tasks.statement: check_eq<T: PartialEq + Debug>(left, right) → Result<(), String> "left: <l:?>, right: <r:?>" when not equal. check_close(a, b, eps) → Result<(), String> "|a-b| = <d> > <eps>". check_sorted<T: PartialOrd + Debug>(v) → Result<(), String> «not sorted at position <i>: <a:?> > <b:?>» (the index of the first violating pair). All checks are functions and do not panic.
tasks.hint: Build the message with format! and {:?}; windows(2) gives the index of the first violation.

tasks.title: Write tests: abs and its mutants
tasks.statement: You need to write failures_abs(f: &dyn Fn(i32) → i32) → usize — a set of checks for the absolute value function: return the number of failed checks. The driver runs your set on a correct implementation (it must give 0 failures) and on five broken ones — each must be caught by at least one failure.
tasks.hint: Check zero, plus and minus one, ordinary numbers of both signs and very large ones in absolute value — each mutant breaks at its own boundary.

tasks.title: Write tests: leap year
tasks.statement: failures_leap(f: &dyn Fn(i32) → bool) → usize — checks for is_leap_year. The correct implementation: divisible by 4, except multiples of 100, except multiples of 400. The driver checks that the correct implementation gives 0 failures and that all four mutants are caught.
tasks.hint: You need years of different kinds: an ordinary leap year, an ordinary non-leap year, a multiple of 100, a multiple of 400 and a multiple of 200 but not 400.

tasks.title: Write tests: clamp(x, lo, hi)
tasks.statement: failures_clamp(f: &dyn Fn(i32, i32, i32) → i32) → usize — checks for clamp(x, lo, hi) = x clipped to [lo, hi] (assume lo ≤ hi). The correct implementation gives 0 failures; the four mutants must be caught.
tasks.hint: Check inside the range, exactly on both boundaries, beyond each boundary, the degenerate range lo = hi and negative boundaries.

tasks.title: Write tests: stack implementations
tasks.statement: The trait StackLike: new() → Self, push(&mut self, i32), pop(&mut self) → Option<i32>, peek(&self) → Option<i32>, len(&self) → usize. Write failures<S: StackLike>() → usize: checks for any implementation. The driver supplies a correct stack and three broken ones (a queue instead of a stack; pop does not decrease the length; peek removes the element) — all must be caught.
tasks.hint: Check LIFO order on several elements, the length after each operation, an empty stack, and that peek removes nothing.

tasks.title: Parsing "1h30m15s": a table of cases
tasks.statement: parse_duration(s) → Option<u64> — seconds: the units h (3600), m (60), s (1), each at most once and in the order h, m, s; the number is unsigned and non-empty. "90s" → 90, "1h30m15s" → 5415, "2h" → 7200. An empty string, a number without a unit, an unknown unit, a repeat or a wrong order → None.
tasks.hint: Accumulate digits in a string; on meeting a letter, turn the accumulated number into seconds and check the order of units.

tasks.title: Library errors: enum, Display, Error, From
tasks.statement: ConfigError: Missing(String) — a missing key, BadNumber { key: String, source: ParseIntError }. Implement Display («no key X» / «key X: invalid number») and std::error::Error with the method source (for BadNumber — the cause, for Missing — None). load(text) → Result<Settings, ConfigError>: lines key=value; port and workers are required (numbers u16 and u8).
tasks.hint: source() returns Some(source) as &dyn Error; for u16 and u8 the numbers 70000 and 256 are already a parse error.

tasks.title: A module tree from paths
tasks.statement: render_tree(paths: &[&str]) → String: paths like "net::tcp::connect" are assembled into a tree; each level is on a separate line indented by two spaces per depth, children alphabetically, duplicates merged. An empty list gives an empty string.
tasks.hint: The tree is nested BTreeMaps (or a node with a BTreeMap of children); entry(...).or_default() creates the missing levels.

tasks.title: The public surface: what is visible outside
tasks.statement: An item is described by a path and the visibility of each segment: Item { path: &str (separated by ::), vis: Vec<Vis> } with Vis ∈ {Private, Crate, Pub} (the lengths are equal). surface(items) → (Vec<String>, Vec<String>): the first is items visible to other crates (all segments Pub), the second is visible only inside the crate (no Private, but at least one Crate). Both lists alphabetical.
tasks.hint: An item is visible from outside only if all segments of the path are open: one private parent is enough to hide a descendant.
